title: Native run crash, recovery and ownership coherence
description: Replay the incident through disposable production gateway RPCs, prove adapter selection through the CLI and verify that child-only regressions fail the corresponding claim. Every driver creates its own state and cleans up only its fixture resources.

incident.intent: Prove signal and redacted crash evidence, blocked conversation recovery, durable busy steering, stopped-worker adoption, normal task completion, foreign-slot preservation and pre-written runtime through gateway RPCs.

legacy.intent: Reload a fixture host from a legacy journal, prove ordinary recovery refuses unknown descendants, then explicitly attest stop and resume the exact conversation.

kernel-reuse.intent: Reload a stopped worker journal whose PID now names a real foreign process, verify the recorded kernel birth proves reuse, and recover without signalling that current owner.

adapters.intent: Execute canonical and legacy custom-adapter references through the CLI and inspect the selected variant's side effect.

cleanup-guards.intent: Prove historical and unsupported-pane preservation, foreign handoff protection, failure settlement despite notification errors, and boot/cleanup process identity boundaries through gateway RPCs.

provider-recovery.intent: Prove legacy and out-of-band provider recovery through explicit operator endpoints, child lease attribution, and identity-preserving rollback when boot metadata fails.

held-reconcile.intent: Restart only the disposable gateway with reconciliation enabled and prove foreign workspace holds survive startup and a real periodic tick.

park-claim.intent: Park through the production gateway, introduce a competing workspace occupant at restore's claim boundary, and preserve the held row, epoch and workspace.

generation-guard.intent: Change the stored generation during verified stopping of a real saved conversation; prove the frozen ownership fence refuses exit and preserves its live process.

queued-receipt.intent: Queue steering during a busy task, close its worker before submission, and assert the interrupted receipt remains readable through the task-scoped gateway endpoint.

authored-contract.intent: Dispatch an authored task whose terminal contract is missing, reconstruct the runtime through the gateway, and preserve its authored report and learning paths.

controls.intent: Disable each repaired path only in a disposable child and require both a mutation receipt and failure of the intended claim.

real-adoption.intent: Use a fresh, read-only installed runner in a disposable profile; assert its native resume hook and saved conversation, adopt through the gateway, then complete and preserve the operator session.
